subject: Request: model artifact pin for Cleantek Private deployment
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena@cleantek.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cleantek.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo — exact artifact pin request for Private deployment

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — the latency numbers look promising. Procurement and engineering at Cleantek have one firm requirement for our private/on-prem deployment: we need the ability to pin an exact model artifact (weights + tokenizer + config) by SHA256 and ensure that the runtime will not silently switch to a different build or quantization at deploy time.

Specifically:
- Target artifact: "phoenix-3.2.1" (we will supply the expected sha256).
- Supported runtime variants: float16 and INT8 quantized. We need compatibility evidence for both (in particular, we cannot accept a silent INT8 fallback without explicit signoff).
- Audit: a machine-readable signed record of which artifact hash served each request for our Private control plane.

Attached are our integration requirements and a short procurement note. Can Redwood confirm whether a model pin (not just version aliasing) is possible in Private? If not, what compensating controls are available (e.g., immutable artifact pins + attestations + forced fallback policy)?

We'd like to align on timeline — procurement is aiming to close the PO by end of August.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ramos
Head of Platform Integrations, Cleantek Systems
attachments: cleantek_integration_requirements.pdf

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena@cleantek.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo — exact artifact pin request for Private deployment

Folks — forwarding Cleantek's ask. TL;DR: customer requires an immutable artifact pin (sha256) for phoenix-3.2.1 and explicit control around quantized variants; procurement timeline end of August.

Questions / asks:
1) Is there an approved process for granting a model-artifact pin in Redwood Private? I know we support pinning by model version, but our gating typically allows patch roll-forwards. Cleantek is asking for a strict immutable artifact pin + audit log.
2) What are the blocking risks for supporting both float16 and INT8 artifacts (runtime compatibility, KV-cache differences, perf regression risk)?
3) If we need an exception to the standard model-compatibility gate, what minimal smoke tests / rollback controls would you require to approve?

I attached the Cleantek spec. Elena — we may loop infra/product for a short checklist this week. I suspect we can do this but want to be explicit about the controls we need to avoid surprises in production.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: cleantek_artifact_spec_v1.pdf

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Elena Ramos <elena@cleantek.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo — exact artifact pin request for Private deployment

Thanks for the context. Short answers first: yes we can pin to a SHA256 artifact in Private if we treat it as a special immutable release and block automated roll-forwards; we do not currently expose a one-click audit-proof signed attestation for every request, but we can produce request-level artifact hashes in logs exported to the customer's log sink (and add a signed metadata blob if needed).

Technical notes / constraints:
- INT8 vs float16: INT8 variants can change token probabilities slightly; we must run a targeted quality smoke-suite (1000 prompt seeds provided by Cleantek) and compare perplexity and a small set of QA prompts. Expect minor semantic deltas; acceptable thresholds must be agreed.
- KV-cache: different kernel paths for quantized kernels — existing KV cache migration is safe but we should force a cold-cache canary for 48 hours in staging to validate continuity for stateful chat sessions.
- Runtime: we'll need a CI artifact that includes both variants (weights+tokenizer+runtime flags) and a lightweight signature file. The Private control plane will honor exact sha256 if marked immutable; we'll have to flip off automatic variant substitution and any model sharding roll-forward behavior.

Required deliverables from Cleantek to proceed to approval:
- The exact sha256 for phoenix-3.2.1 (weights + tokenizer + config separated)
- The 1k prompts for smoke testing (or permission to sample from production-like prompts)
- Acceptance thresholds for generation QA (top-line: pass rate >= 95% on safety & correctness checks and <= 5% of responses with significant semantic drift)

Operational asks from Product/Infra (Lauren / Grace):
- A canary rollout plan (percentage + duration) and explicit rollback triggers (latency regressions, error rate > X, QA regressions).
- A requirement that the artifact pin is only applied to Cleantek's Private cluster and not to shared Hosted routes.

I can spin up a smoke-run and produce a short compatibility report in ~4 business days once we have the sha256 and prompt set.

- Dev

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Elena Ramos <elena@cleantek.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo — exact artifact pin request for Private deployment

Agree with Dev's plan. Approve exception to standard variant roll-forward for Cleantek under the following conditions:

1) Canary: 5% traffic for 72 hours in their Private cluster, followed by 25% for 72 hours, then 100% if no regressions.
2) Rollback triggers: >=2% increase in 99th percentile token latency, error rate >1% on the route, or QA fail rate exceeding the threshold Dev outlined.
3) Audit & attestation: Infra to provide a signed metadata blob on release (we can reuse our release signing process) and enable request-level artifact hash logging to the customer's log sink.
4) Security review: security to sign off on the attestation format — Grace, can you shepherd?

Connor — please confirm we have the sha256 + the prompt set and ask Cleantek to confirm acceptance thresholds in writing. Once we have the smoke-run report, I'll schedule a 30-min final alignment with Procurement + Engineering and ship the exception.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ramos <elena@cleantek.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, procurement@cleantek.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo — exact artifact pin request for Private deployment

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary / next steps:

- Redwood can support an immutable artifact pin for phoenix-3.2.1 in your Private cluster. Our Product team has approved an exception to disable automatic variant roll-forward for this customer only, with the canary and rollback triggers described below.
- Action items for Cleantek (please reply on-thread):
  * Provide the sha256 for weights + tokenizer + config (single string per artifact).
  * Share the 1k prompt seeds (or confirm we can sample).
  * State acceptance thresholds in writing (safety, correctness percentage).
  * Procurement: confirm target PO date (you had end of August).

- Internal action items (cc'd):
  * Dev: run smoke-suite once sha256 + prompts arrive; deliver compatibility report (aim +4 business days).
  * Grace / Infra: prepare signed release metadata and request-level artifact hash logging to the customer's log sink; security sign-off required.
  * Lauren: finalize canary schedule in runbook link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/CLEANTEK-rollback

I've attached a short smoke-test-plan template. We'll tentatively schedule the final alignment meeting for Aug 1st; if procurement needs a PO earlier we'll accelerate.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: smoke-test-plan.md
